items.name: Soul Monger
items.summary: Medium humanoid (elf); CR 11.

rawJson.name: Soul Monger
rawJson.summary: Medium humanoid (elf); CR 11.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.summary: The soul monger has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Soul Thirst
traits.summary: When the soul monger reduces a creature to 0 hit points, the soul monger can gain temporary hit points equal to half the creature's hit point maximum. While the soul monger has temporary hit points from this ability, it has advantage on attack rolls.

traits.name: Weight of Ages
traits.summary: Any beast or humanoid, other than a shadar-kai, that starts its turn within 5 feet of the soul monger has its speed reduced by 20 feet until the start of that crea- ture's next turn. ..

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.summary: The soul monger has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put it to sleep.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.summary: The soul monger's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast these spells, requiring no material components: at will: chill touch (3d8 damage), poison spray (3d12 damage); 1/day each: bestow curse, chain lightning, finger of death, gaseous form, phantasmal killer, seeming.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: The soul monger makes two phantasmal dag- ger attacks.

actions.name: Phantasmal Dagger
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (4d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 19 (3d12) necrotic damage, and the target has disadvantage on saving throws until the start of the soul monger's next turn.

actions.name: Wave of Weariness (Recharge 4-6)
actions.summary: The soul monger emits weariness in a 60-foot cube. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 45 (10d8) psychic damage and suffers 1 level of exhaustion. On a successful save, it takes 22 (5d8) psychic damage.

items.name: Spirit Troll
items.summary: Large giant; CR 11.

rawJson.name: Spirit Troll
rawJson.summary: Large giant; CR 11.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.summary: The troll can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage ifit ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.summary: The troll regains 10 hit points at the start of each of its turns. If the troll takes psychic or force damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: The troll makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 19 (3d10 + 3) psychic damage, and the target must suc- ceed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be stunned for 1 min- ute. The stunned target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Claws
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) psychic damage.

traits.name: Return to Worms
traits.summary: When the larva mage is reduced to 0 hit points, it breaks apart into a swarm ofinsects in the same space. Unless the swarm is destroyed, the larva mage reforms from it 24 hours later.

resistances: and slashing while in dim light or darkness

traits.name: Wretched Pack Tactics
traits.summary: The Wretched has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the Wretched's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't inca- pacitated. The Wretched otherwise has disadvantage on at- tack rolls.

actions.name: Bite
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d10 + l) piercing damage, and the Wretched attaches to the target. While attached, the Wretched can't attack, and at the start of each of the Wretched's turns, the target takes 6 (1d10 + 1) necrotic damage. The attached Wretched moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the Wretched's movement. The Wretched can detach itself by spending S feet of its movement on its turn. A creature, including the target, can use its action to detach a Wretched.

items.summary: Medium fiend (devil); CR 16.

rawJson.name: Titivilus
rawJson.summary: Medium fiend (devil); CR 16.

resistances: and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.summary: Titivilus's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 21). He can innately cast these spells, requiring no material components: at will: alter self, animate dead, bestow curse, confusion, major image, modify memory, nondetection, sending, suggestion; 3/day each: greater invisibility (self only), mislead; 1/day each: feeblemind, symbol (discord or sleep only).

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.summary: lfTitivilus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.summary: Titivilus has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Magic Weapons
traits.summary: Titivilus's weapon attacks are magical.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.summary: Titivilus regains 10 hit points at the start of his turn. lfhe takes cold or radiant damage, this trait doesn't func· ti on at the start of his next turn. Titivilus dies only if he starts his turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Ventriloquism
traits.summary: Whenever Titivilus speaks, he can choose a point within 60 feet; his voice emanates from that point.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: Titivilus makes one sword attack and uses his Frightful Word once.

actions.name: Silver Sword
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands, plus 16 (3d10) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to half the necrotic damage it takes.

actions.name: Frightful Word
actions.summary: Titivilus targets one creature he can see within 10 feet of him. The target must succeed on a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of him for 1 minute. While frightened in this way, the target must take the Dash action and move away from Titivilus by the safest available route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Teleport
actions.summary: Titivilus magically teleports, along with any equipment he is wearing and carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space he can see.

actions.name: Twisting Words
actions.summary: Titivilus targets one creature he can see within 60 feet of him. The target must succeed on a DC 21 Charisma saving throw or become charmed by Titivilus for 1 minute. The charmed target can repeat the saving throw if Titivilus deals any damage to hit. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to Titivilus's Twisting Words for 24 hours.

rawJson.name: Sibriex: Flesh Warping Variant
rawJson.summary: Optional flesh-warping procedure and d100 transformation table associated with a sibriex.

mechanics.trigger: A sibriex can use Warp Creature to alter a creature; the variant also permits a creature to willingly submit to flesh warping.
mechanics.sourceTableText:
Keepers of Forbidden Lore. Sibriexes have spent 
eons amassing information from across the planes, 
hoarding knowledge for when it might be useful. Such 
is their incredible intellect that many seek them out, in-
cluding demon lords. Some sibriexes act as advisors and 
oracles, manipulating demons into serving their ends, 
while other sibriexes cling to their secrets, parceling out 
lore only when doing so would advance their plans. 
Dem on Grafters. Sibriexes can channel the power of 
the Abyss to create new demons from other creatures. 
Over the course of days, they can create vast numbers 
of rutterkins to protect their lands and to ensure that 
the plane teems with destructive monsters. Some de-
mons petition sibriexes for physical gifts, and if they are 
moved to do so, sibriexes can graft on new body parts 
to give the demons greater strength, vision, or stamina. 
Sibriexes never give aid freely; they demand a service or 
a treasure in return for the flesh-shaping they provide. 
VARIANT: FLESH WARPING 
Creatures that encounter a sibriex can be twisted be-
yond recognition. Whenever a creature fails a saving 
throw against the sibriex's Warp Creature effect, you 
can roll percentile dice and consult the Flesh Warping 
table to determine an additional effect, which vanishes 
when Warp Creature ends on the creature. If the crea-
ture transforms into an abyssal wretch, the effect be-
comes a permanent feature of that body. 
A creature can willingly submit to flesh warping, an 
agonizing process that takes at least 1 hour while the 
creature stays within 30 feet of the sibriex. At the end 
of the process, roll once on the table (or choose one 
effect) to determine how the creature is transformed 
permanently. 
FL ES H W ARPIN G 
dlOO 
Effect 
01-05 
The color of the target's hair, eyes, and skin be-
comes blue, red, yellow, or patterned. 
06-10 
The target's eyes push out of its head at the end of 
stalks. 
11-15 
The target's hands grow claws, which can be used 
as daggers. 
16-20 
One of the target's legs grows longer than the 
other, reducing its walking speed by 10 feet. 
21- 25 
The target's eyes become beacons, filling a l 5-foot 
cone with dim light when they are open. 
26- 30 
A pair of wings, either feathered or leathery, sprout 
from the target's back, granting it a flying speed of 
30 feet. 
31- 35 
The target's ears tear free from its head and scurry 
away; the target is deafened. 
36- 40 
Two of the target's teeth turn into tusks. 
41-45 
The

gnoll, towering 14 feet tall. Yeenoghu is the Gnoll Lord, 
and his creations are made in his twisted image. When 
the demon lord hunted across the Material Plane, packs 
of hyenas followed in his wake. Those that ate of great 
Yeenoghu's kills became gnolls, emulating their mas-
ter's ways. Few others worship the Beast of Butchery, 
but those who do tend to take on a gnoll-like aspect, 
hunched over, and filing their teeth down to points. 
Yeenoghu wants nothing more than slaughter and 
senseless destruction. The gnolls are his instruments, 
and he drives them to ever-greater atrocities in his 
name. Yeenoghu takes pleasure in causing fear before 
death, and he sows sorrow and despair through destroy-
ing beloved things. He doesn't parlay; to meet him is 
to do battle with him- unless he becomes bored. The 
Beast of Butchery has a long rivalry with Baphomet, the 
Horned King, and the two demon lords and their follow-
ers attack one another on sight. 
The Gnoll Lord is covered in matted fur and taut, 
leathery hide, his face like a grinning predator's skull. 
Patchwork armor made of discarded shields and 
breastplates is lashed onto his body with heavy chains, 
decorated by the flayed skins of his foes. He wields a 
triple-headed flail called the Butcher, which he can sum-
mon into his hand at will, although he is as likely to tear 
his prey apart with his bare hands before ripping out its 
throat with his teeth.

Yeenoghu's lair in the Abyss is called the Death Dells, 
its barren hills and ravines serving as one great hunting 
ground, where he pursues captured mortals in a cruel 
game. Yeenoghu's lair is a place of blood and death, 
populated by gnolls, hyenas, and ghouls, and there are 
few structures or signs of civilization on his layer of 
the Abyss. 
LAIR ACTIONS 
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), Yeenoghu 
can take a lair action to cause one of the following 
effects; he can't use the same effect two rounds in a row: 
• Yeenoghu causes an iron spike- 5 feet tall and 1 inch 
in diameter-to burst from the ground at a point he 
can see within 100 feet of him. Any creature in the 
space where the spike emerges must make a DC 24 
Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature 
takes 27 (6d8) piercing damage and is restrained by 
being impaled on the spike. A creature can use an 
action to remove itself (or a creature it can reach) from 
the spike, ending the restrained condition. 

• Each gnoll or hyena that Yeenoghu can see can use its 
reaction to move up to its speed. 
• Until the next initiative count 20, all gnolls and hye-
nas within the lair are enraged, causing them to have 
advantage on melee weapon attack rolls and causing 
attack rolls to have advantage against them. 
REGIONAL EFFECTS 
The region containing Yeenoghu's lair is warped by his 
magic, creating one or more of the following effects: 
• Within 1 mile of the lair, large iron spikes grow out of 
the ground and stone surfaces. Yeenoghu impales the 
bodies of the slain on these spikes. 
• Predatory beasts within 6 miles of the lair become un-
usually savage, killing far more than what they need 
for food. Carcasses of prey are left to rot in an unnatu-
ral display of wasteful slaughter. 
• If a humanoid spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile 
of the lair, that creature must succeed on a DC 17 
Wisdom saving throw or descend into a madness 
determined by the Madness of Yeenoghu table. A 
creature that succeeds on this saving throw can't be 
affected by this regional effect again for 24 hours.

mechanics.sourceRuleText:
Zuggtmoy's principal lair is her palace on Shedaklah. 
It consists of two dozen mushrooms of pale yellow and 
rancid brown. These massive fungi are some of the larg-
est in existence. They are surrounded by a field of acidic 
puffballs and poisonous vapors. The mushrooms are all 
interconnected by bridges of shelf-fungi, and countless 
chambers have been hollowed out inside their rubbery, 
fibrous stalks. 
LAIR ACTIONS 
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), 
Zuggtmoy can take a lair action to cause one of the 
following effects; she can't use the same effect two 
rounds in a row: 
• Zuggtmoy causes four gas spores or violet fungi 
(see the Monster Manual) to appear in unoccupied 
spaces that she chooses within the lair. They vanish 
after 1 hour. 
• Up to four plant creatures that are friendly to Zuggt-
moy and that Zuggtmoy can see can use their re-
actions to move up to their speed and make one 
weapon attack. 
• Zuggtmoy uses either her Infestation Spores or her 
Mind Control Spores, centered on a mushroom or 
other fungus within her lair, instead of on herself. 
REGIONAL EFFECTS 
The region containing Zuggtmoy's lair is warped by her 
magic, creating one or more of the following effects: 
• Molds and fungi grow on surfaces within 6 miles 
of the lair, even where they would normally find 
no purchase. 
• Plant life within 1 mile of the lair becomes in-
fested with parasitic fungi, slowly mutating as it is 
overwhelmed. 

• If a humanoid spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile 
of the lair, that creature must succeed on a DC 17 
Wisdom saving throw or descend into a madness 
determined by the Madness of Zuggtmoy table. A 
creature that succeeds on this saving throw can't be 
affected by this regional effect again for 24 hours. 
If Zuggtmoy dies, these effects fade over the course of 
ldlO days. 
MADNESS OF ZUGGTMOY 
If a creature goes mad in Zuggtmoy's lair or within 
line of sight of the demon lord, roll on the Madness of 
Zuggtmoy table to determine the nature of the madness, 
which is a character flaw that lasts until cured. See the 
Du11geon Master's Guide for more on madness.

items.name: Belashyrra
items.summary: Medium Aberration; CR 22.

rawJson.name: Belashyrra
rawJson.summary: Medium Aberration; CR 22.

traits.name: Alien Mind
traits.summary: If a creature tries to read Belashyrra's thoughts or deals psychic damage to it, that creature must succeed on a DC 22 Intelligence saving throw or be stunned for 1 minute. The stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Eye Thief
traits.summary: Belashyrra can see through the eyes of all creatures within 120 feet of it. It can use its Eye Ray through any creature within 120 feet of it, as though it were in that creature's space.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.summary: If Belashyrra fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.summary: Belashyrra has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.summary: Belashyrra regains 20 hit points at the start of its turn. If it takes radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. Belashyrra dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Teleport
traits.summary: As a bonus action, Belashyrra can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: Belashyrra makes two attacks with its claws and uses its Eye Ray once.

actions.name: Claw
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: + 14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d6 + 7) slashing damage.

actions.name: Eye Ray

items.name: Dyrrn

traits.name: Alien Mind
traits.summary: If a creature tries to read Dyrrn's thoughts or deals psychic damage to it, that creature must succeed on a DC 23 Intelligence saving throw or be stunned for 1 minute. The stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.summary: If Dyrrn fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.summary: Dyrrn has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.summary: Dyrrn regains 20 hit points at the start of its turn. If Dyrrn takes radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. Dyrrn dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Teleport
traits.summary: As a bonus action, Dyrrn can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: Dyrrn makes one Tentacle Whip attack and uses its Corruption once. Dyrrn can replace its Tentacle Whip attack with Extract Brain if it has a creature grappled.

actions.name: Tentacle Whip
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 23), pulled into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of Dyrrn, and must succeed on a DC 23 Intelligence saving throw or be stunned until this grapple ends. Dyrrn can't use the same ten tacle whip on another target until this grapple ends. Dyrrn has two tentacle whips.

actions.name: Corruption
actions.summary: Dyrrn targets one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 23 Constitution saving throw or take 22 (4d6 + 8) necrotic damage and become cor rupted for 1 minute. A corrupted creature's flesh twists in alien ways. The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls, its speed is reduced by half, and if it tries to cast a spell, it must first succeed on a DC 15 In telligence check or the spell fails and is wasted. The corrupted creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Extract Brain
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +15 to hit, reach 5 ft., one incapacitated creature grappled by Dyrrn. Hit: 55 (lOdlO) pierc ing damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, Dyrrn kills the target by extracting and devouring its brain.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.summary: The soldier has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the soldier's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

traits.name: Undead Nature
traits.summary: A Karrnathi undead soldier doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

traits.name: Undead Fortitude
traits.summary: If damage reduces the soldier to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the soldier drops to 1 hit point instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: The soldier attacks three times with one of its weapons.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one tar get. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (ldlO + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Longbow

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.summary: The soldier adds 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the soldier must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

rawJson.name: Warforged Colossus
rawJson.summary: Gargantuan Construct; CR 25.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.summary: The colossus is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.summary: If the colossus fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.summary: The colossus has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.summary: The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

traits.name: Towering Terror
traits.summary: Any enemy outside the colossus that starts its turn within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 26 Wisdom sav· ing throw or be frightened until the start of the enemy's next turn. If the enemy's saving throw is successful, it is immune to this colossus's Towering Terror for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: The colossus makes three attacks-one with its slam and two with its eldritch turrets-and then uses Stomp.

actions.name: Slam
actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 29 (3d12 + 10) bludgeoning damage, and the colossus can push the target up to 20 feet away from it.

actions.name: Eldritch Turret
actions.summary: Ranged Spell Attack: +18 to hit, range 300 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (4d8) force damage, and ifthe target is a creature, it is knocked prone.

actions.name: Stomp
actions.summary: The colossus stomps one of its feet at a point on the ground within 20 feet of it. Any creature in a 20-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder centered on this point must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity saving throw or take 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage and fal l prone. Until the colossus uses its Stomp again or moves, the creature is restrained. While restrained in this way, the creature (or another creature within 5 feet of it) can use its action to make a DC 26 Strength check. On a success, the creature relocates to an unoccupied space of its choice within 5 feet of the colossus and is no longer restrained. Structures, as well as nonmagical objects that are neither be ing worn nor carried, take the same amount of damage if they are in the cylinder (no save).

actions.name: Incinerating Beam (Recharge 5-6)
actions.summary: The colossus fires a beam of light in a 150-foot line that is 10 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 26 Dexterity saving throw, taking 60 (l l dl O) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this beam is disintegrated, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

Transform immediately into a random Beast CR 5 or lower for 2d12 days; game statistics are replaced, nonmagical worn/carried gear melds, magic items drop within 5 feet; form cannot otherwise be altered, but Wish can end it early.
Gain ability to speak, read, and write 1d6 + 2 languages of your choice.
Gain ability to cast Time Stop 1d3 times; choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as spellcasting ability.
Immediately gain the benefits of finishing a long rest.
Gain climbing speed equal to walking speed and can move on vertical surfaces and ceilings with hands free.
Sprout softly luminescent feathered wings and gain flying speed 30 feet.
A homunculus appears within 5 feet; DM determines appearance and it treats you as its creator.
Drop to 0 HP, become unconscious, and begin death saves. Magical healing cannot restore HP until stabilized. After three failed death saves, resurrection is possible only by Wish.
Roll d20: even ages you 1d10 years; odd makes you 1d10 years younger, minimum age 1. Only Wish, divine intervention, or similar magic can undo it.
Gain ability to cast Gate 1d4 times without material components; choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as spellcasting ability.
A dragon egg appears and immediately hatches into a DM-chosen dragon wyrmling; it views you as its parent and is staunchly loyal to you and allies.
Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder; gain immunity to that damage type.
Dexterity increases by 2, maximum 22.
A fey crossing opens and pulls you into the Feywild; you draw no more cards. Crossing remains open 1 minute; destination is chosen by DM.

A powerful Fiend appears nearby and offers a deal; DM defines terms. It is indifferent and keeps bargains though it can twist wording. If attacked or negotiations fail and offer is refused, it returns home.
Grow 2d10 inches taller; maximum and current HP each increase by 20.
You can immediately stop drawing regardless of declared number.
All ability scores increase by 1, maximum 20.
Intelligence increases by 2, maximum 22.

Within 1 year, once mentally name/describe a familiar object or individual; know location and distance even across planes. For an individual, know alive status and conditions; for object, know if broken; for charged magic item, know remaining charges.
Gain 1d3 levels of exhaustion.
2d6 gems worth 5,000 gp each and 1d10 chunks of precious ore worth 2,500 gp each appear.
DM-chosen Large or larger Monstrosity CR 10 or lower appears within 15 feet, hostile and attacks immediately; disappears when killed or when you reach 0 HP. No effect if insufficient space.
A gelatinous cube appears in your space and engulfs you; hostile until destroyed. No effect if insufficient space.
Walking speed increases by 10 feet.
Pit opens beneath you; fall 3d6 × 10 feet, take falling damage, and become prone.

Gain ability to cast Speak with Plants without a slot once per long rest; if you have 3rd-level+ slots, you can also cast it with them. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as spellcasting ability.
Wisdom increases by 2, maximum 22.

Magic-force chains restrain you; you cannot cast spells and carried/worn magic-item properties are suppressed; draw no more cards. Chains are damage-immune and cannot be dispelled; Disintegrate destroys them; another creature can free you with DC 30 Dexterity check using thieves' tools.
A DM-chosen rare-or-rarer magic ring appears on your finger; if an attunement slot is available, you automatically attune.
A DM-chosen rare-or-rarer magic armor you are proficient with appears. If you have no armor proficiency, base AC becomes 12 + Dexterity modifier while unarmored.
Gain proficiency in three skills chosen by the DM.
A DM-chosen rare-or-rarer magic rod, staff, or wand appears in your hands.
Choose either reduce declared draws by two or receive a DM-chosen rare-or-rarer wondrous item.
Immediately become petrified as marble until freed by Greater Restoration or similar magic.
Charisma increases by 2, maximum 22.

A deity/similar power is bound to aid you once before death: use an action to call for DM-defined divine intervention; if unused when you die, it instead casts Resurrection on you; obligation then ends.
Within 1 year, cast True Resurrection once without a spell slot or material components; choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as spellcasting ability.
Draw two extra cards; their magic is delayed. Choose one to keep and return the other; chosen card then takes effect.
Skin becomes barklike; base AC 15 + Dexterity modifier while unarmored, but gain fire vulnerability. Only Wish, divine intervention, or similar magic reverses it.
A revenant rises somewhere on Material Plane, blames you, and hunts you until 1 year passes, it kills you, or Wish banishes it permanently.
Strength increases by 2, maximum 22.
Learn three cantrips of your choice from any spell list.

items.summary: Twelve constellation-driven regional mechanical effects from the Sky of Many Things.

rawJson.name: Sky of Many Things Zodiac Phenomena
rawJson.summary: Twelve constellation-driven regional mechanical effects from the Sky of Many Things.

activeConstellationEffects.effect: At dusk each day, Undead in the region gain 13 (3d8) temporary hit points.
Each creature intuitively knows the damage immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities of any creature it sees.
Creatures have advantage on Charisma checks made to improve another creature’s attitude.
Creatures are immune to the frightened condition.
A creature can unlock an object merely by touching it, including magically locked objects.
When a creature fails a Charisma check made to improve another creature’s attitude, the target becomes hostile if it was not already hostile.

When a non-evil adventuring party outdoors enters combat, spectral knights aid them; on initiative count 20 (losing ties), each enemy of the characters takes 9 (2d8) force damage. The knights vanish when combat ends.

Vegetation is difficult terrain and poisonous. Entering it or ending a turn there requires DC 12 CON save; failure deals 7 (2d6) poison damage. If this damage would reduce a creature to 0 HP, it instead drops to 1 HP and is petrified until Greater Restoration or similar magic.
Creatures have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
At midnight on a clear night, silver coins worth 100 gp fall scattered through the region.
Common magic items, cantrips, and 1st-level spells do not function in the region.
When a Humanoid rolls a natural 1 on an ability check or attack roll, it becomes incapacitated until the end of its next turn as it laughs uncontrollably.

rawJson.name: House of Cards Card Challenges
rawJson.summary: Structured mechanical challenges tied to card-themed rooms in the House of Cards.

challenges.formationCheck: Dexterity or Intelligence check with jeweler’s or mason’s tools, or melee attack roll

challenges.effect: Conversing with reflection requires DC 12 Wisdom save or 2d4 psychic damage.
Hot ceiling deals 2d10 fire damage per round to affected creatures.
Concentrate for 10 minutes to reproduce Contact Other Plane and its risks; DC 18 Intelligence (Arcana) identifies the effect.

Corridor is difficult terrain. When a creature starts its turn or uses movement/action/bonus action/reaction, a trap makes +7 ranged attack to 60 feet; hit 4d10 necrotic. If wearing nonmagical armor/shield, random eligible item takes permanent cumulative -1 AC; armor at AC 10 or shield bonus 0 is destroyed. Dispel Magic DC 15 disables traps for 1 minute.
Avatar of Death binds to first creature that responds/attacks/opens door; hostile actions or healing can spawn separate bound avatars. Door remains closed until all avatars are destroyed.
Apparition answers one question using Divination-like guidance without random card reading.
First sitter gains Charm of the Throne; while it lasts has disadvantage on Charisma checks and expects obedience. Once only; Remove Curse can remove.
Basin causes 2d6 necrotic damage and equal max-HP reduction until long rest. First use reveals Throne secret door, second within 10 minutes reveals Knight, third reveals Key.

destroyOptions: any 3rd-level-or-higher spell creating bright light while chains are in bright light

challenges.effect: Medusa’s dying curse gives creatures that attacked/damaged her disadvantage on checks and saves using their highest ability. Cannot be broken while House exists; afterward Remove Curse or similar magic can end it.
Air elemental variant immune to cold; if one character defeats it without aid, that character immediately gains benefits of a long rest.

Thought-based flight speed 30 if no other flight. Mist edge wraps to opposite side. Taking mask requires DC 15 CHA save, with disadvantage while Breath Drinker lives. Replacing soul-mask restores soul and starts collapse.

items.name: Creating a Deck of Many More Things Card
items.summary: Level-17+ guidelines for inventing a new card for the Deck of Many More Things, including optional creator rewards and intentionally open-ended crafting requirements.

rawJson.name: Creating a Deck of Many More Things Card
rawJson.summary: Level-17+ guidelines for inventing a new card for the Deck of Many More Things, including optional creator rewards and intentionally open-ended crafting requirements.

mechanics.restriction: The Deck of Many More Things itself cannot be crafted by these guidelines; a campaign can instead allow creation of a new card for its complement.
mechanics.formula: No existing formula; the creator must invent one.
mechanics.creationTime: Unspecified; source says it should take a very long time and could take years.
mechanics.ingredients: Rare/high-risk magical ingredients are expected; the ritual can require exact circumstances or divine intervention. No fixed list is supplied.

optionalCreatorRewards.name: Demiplane
optionalCreatorRewards.effect: Creating the card simultaneously creates a demiplane inspired by that card; the creator has complete control over it and can use it as a home.

optionalCreatorRewards.name: Exclusive Membership
optionalCreatorRewards.effect: Creation can grant entry to a secret cabal whose members gather yearly; this is a campaign privilege rather than a numeric bonus.

optionalCreatorRewards.name: Immortality
optionalCreatorRewards.effect: Creator stops aging and cannot die of old age until the created card or a Deck of Many Things containing it is destroyed. If that happens, the missed years immediately catch up, likely killing the creator.

optionalCreatorRewards.name: World Walking
optionalCreatorRewards.effect: Creator can travel to any world where the created card has manifested as part of a Deck of Many Things.

items.name: Inspiration Hand
items.summary: A twenty-two-card subsystem that turns inspiration into a shared hand of one-use tactical card effects.

rawJson.name: Inspiration Hand
rawJson.summary: A twenty-two-card subsystem that turns inspiration into a shared hand of one-use tactical card effects.

mechanics.setup: Draw a number of cards equal to the number of players and place them face up as a communal hand.
mechanics.gainInspiration: Whenever a player gains inspiration, that player must choose a card from the communal hand.
mechanics.useAndReplace: The chosen card is later spent at its listed timing. After it is used, draw a replacement card and shuffle the spent card back into the deck.

cardEffects.effect: Immediately spend one Hit Die; roll it and add CON modifier, regaining that many HP, minimum 1.

cardEffects.target: one creature chosen as your foe
cardEffects.effect: Target is vulnerable to your damage, resistant to all other damage, and has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you. Ends when any creature other than you damages it.
Move to an empty demiplane until end of your next turn; you cannot affect or be affected by the original plane, then return to same or nearest unoccupied space.

cardEffects.trigger: when a creature makes a saving throw
cardEffects.effect: That creature has disadvantage on the save.

cardEffects.trigger: after a single d20 roll you just made
cardEffects.effect: Reroll it and use the second result.
Deal +1d6 fire damage.
The creature that dealt the damage falls prone.
Take one additional action on your turn.
Take the Disengage action.
Teleport yourself and worn/carried equipment up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space.
Impose disadvantage on an attack roll made by a creature you can see.
Regain one expended 1st-level spell slot OR regain one use of an ability that has a limited number of uses per day.
Gain advantage on a saving throw.
Gain advantage on an attack roll.
Target has disadvantage on all ability checks until end of its next turn.
Take the Help or Search action.

cardEffects.duration: until start of your next turn
cardEffects.effect: Deathly shroud; a creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you takes 1d6 necrotic damage.
Gain advantage on an ability check.

cardEffects.trigger: when a melee attack hits you
cardEffects.effect: Attacker is blinded until end of your next turn.
Target’s speed becomes 0 until start of its next turn.
The source of the damage is frightened of you until end of its next turn.
You gain resistance to that damage until start of your next turn.

mechanics.dmVariant: Each time a player spends inspiration, the DM can draw a card, keep it secret, and later play its effect on an opponent; the DM’s card is not added to the communal hand.

items.name: Journey Spread
items.summary: Card-based multi-day travel resolution procedure in which each day has a challenge card and a resulting Reward or Ruin card.

rawJson.name: Journey Spread
rawJson.summary: Card-based multi-day travel resolution procedure in which each day has a challenge card and a resulting Reward or Ruin card.

mechanics.recommendedJourneyLength: approximately at least as many days as there are players
mechanics.setup: For each travel day, lay two face-down cards overlapping. At the start of a day, one player flips the top card; its symbolism inspires that day’s challenge, choice, check, or encounter. That player’s character is the focus.
mechanics.resolution: Success or failure determines whether the lower card is interpreted as Reward or Ruin. Another character may help at DM discretion.

rewards.name: Friendly Aid
rewards.effect: Introduce helpful assistance appropriate to the card and journey.

rewards.name: Ready Foraging
rewards.effect: No ration is needed that day, and each character starts the next day with inspiration.

rewards.name: Reduced Travel Time
rewards.effect: Reduce the journey by 1 day; remove the final pair of cards.

rewards.name: Treasure
rewards.effect: Award card-inspired treasure or use DMG treasure tables.

ruins.name: Encounter
ruins.effect: Introduce an encounter inspired by the card.

ruins.name: Exhaustion
ruins.effect: Each character gains 2 levels of exhaustion.

ruins.name: Extra Travel Time
ruins.effect: Add 1 travel day and two more cards.

ruins.name: Lost Gear
ruins.effect: One character loses suitable gear, rations, or another travel resource.

ruins.name: Restless Night
ruins.effect: The characters are unable to finish a long rest.

items.name: Encounter Deck
items.summary: Reusable deck-building procedure for generating evolving combat and noncombat encounters, including Friend, Lurker, Twin, Draw, Noncombat, and Goal cards.

rawJson.name: Encounter Deck
rawJson.summary: Reusable deck-building procedure for generating evolving combat and noncombat encounters, including Friend, Lurker, Twin, Draw, Noncombat, and Goal cards.

buildGuidelines.recommendedCRRange: roughly half the party level through 2 CR higher than the party level

mechanics.encounterDraw: Shuffle and draw a number of cards equal to the number of characters. Use one or more drawn cards to build the encounter. Afterward, discard cards for monsters that were killed so they do not repeat.
mechanics.groupRule: Cards marked as the same group appear together when two or more members of that group are drawn.
mechanics.multipleRule: One monster card can represent 2-4 weaker monsters.
mechanics.specialCardGuideline: A typical deck of about 20 monster cards can include 3-4 special cards.

specialCards.name: Friend
specialCards.effect: Set aside and draw two additional cards. Friend fights with the characters. Recommended CR is 1-2 lower than party level.

specialCards.name: Lurker
specialCards.effect: Set aside while building normal encounter; lurker arrives separately, beginning as far away as reasonable and preferably hidden.

specialCards.name: Twin
specialCards.effect: Both linked Twin cards must be drawn. If only one appears, shuffle it back and run the remaining encounter. Each Twin is roughly party-level CR.

specialCards.name: Draw Two
specialCards.effect: Discard this card and draw two more; Draw Three/Draw Four variants are possible.

specialCards.name: Noncombat
specialCards.effect: May be used alone as a noncombat encounter or combined with additional normal encounter draws.

specialCards.name: Goal
specialCards.effect: Represents destination/target. If drawn too early, give a hint, draw a replacement, and reshuffle Goal. It can elude the party twice before being reached, or be withheld until a milestone; it can also be a Twin pair.

mechanics.evolvingDeck: Removed cards can be replaced from a second themed deck, or a special trigger can add another deck. A Goal can be inserted only after enough progress.

rawJson.name: Balance and Ruin
rawJson.summary: Tier-2 deadly mechanical balance-beam trap combining counterweights, magnetic walls, and a moving gear pit.

fulcrum.trigger: Weight placed between entrance and fulcrum without sufficient counterweight on the opposite side activates the pressure mechanism; if all weight leaves, the beam remains in its last position.

balanceSave.trigger: creature ends a turn on the beam or is on it when the beam tilts
balanceSave.disadvantageIf: magnetic walls are active and creature wears metal armor or holds a metal object

magneticWalls.targets: creatures not on the beam that wear metal armor or hold a metal object
magneticWalls.effect: Pulled to nearest wall, takes 2d10 bludgeoning damage, and is restrained until field deactivates.
magneticWalls.deactivation: Place appropriate counterweight on opposite side of the beam.
magneticWalls.optionalFlyingVariant: The field can switch every minute or whenever a creature ends its turn on a different side; a flying metal-bearing creature can be pulled to and stuck on a wall.

gearPit.trigger: creature falls into or ends its turn in the moving gears
gearPit.proneRestriction: A prone creature in the gears cannot stand until a creature uses an action to jam the gears with a Tiny object.
gearPit.jam: Lasts through the affected creature’s turn; the Tiny object is lost.

items.summary: Tier-1 dangerous magical trap with constant solar radiation, a grappling talons pedestal, an animated oversized key, and a keyed skull door.

rawJson.name: Surface of the Sun
rawJson.summary: Tier-1 dangerous magical trap with constant solar radiation, a grappling talons pedestal, an animated oversized key, and a keyed skull door.

payload.damageFormula: 1d10 radiant each initiative 20; 2d10 slashing from talons

mechanics.layout: Three parallel halls, each 15 by 100 feet with a 50-foot ceiling; dividing walls are 40 feet high. A gold key is in the right hall, a silver orb in the middle, and a skull-shaped keyhole door in the left.

ambientRadiance.effect: Every creature in the area takes 1d10 radiant damage.

talonsPedestal.object: 1-foot silver orb held by metal talons
talonsPedestal.trigger: Touching or attempting to take the orb
talonsPedestal.effect: Talons snap shut, dealing 2d10 slashing damage and grappling the creature (escape DC 15); the orb is released.

detect.detail: Pressure plate visible through slit on east side

talonsPedestal.reachRestriction: A Medium or Small creature grappled by the talons cannot reach the mechanism.

oversizedKey.animation: One round after removal, the key animates as a Flying Sword and attempts to return to its stand, attacking blockers.
oversizedKey.repair: If reduced to 0 HP, the key must be repaired (for example with Mending) before the skull door works.

mechanics.skullDoor: Insert the oversized key into the skull’s nose and turn it clockwise.

rawJson.name: Test of the Empty Moon
rawJson.summary: Tier-1 setback mechanical weight puzzle using an immovable rod, a 4,000-pound scale threshold, flooding, and four Ochre Jellies.

balanceSave.trigger: entering the bowl or ending a turn inside

bowl.escape: Cannot climb out without assistance; rim is flush with the floor.

immovableRod.deactivation: Lever operates the mechanism/button on the rod.

scaleAndGlyph.openCondition: Portcullis remains open while required weight threshold is met.
scaleAndGlyph.bowlContribution: approximately half the required weight once dropped

mechanics.leverSequence: Pulling the lever deactivates the rod so the bowl drops onto the scale and simultaneously opens sewer valves that release four Ochre Jellies and water.

water.end: When enough total weight completes the glyph, flooding stops and the portcullis opens.

traits.name: Alien Mind

actions.effect: Makes three Whispering Blade attacks and can use Debilitating Touch.

actions.rider: If target is a creature, DC 20 WIS save or it cannot speak until start of corrupter’s next turn.

actions.name: Debilitating Touch
actions.failure: Paralyzed until end of target’s next turn; afterward target is immune to this Debilitating Touch for 24 hours.

bonusActions.name: Change Shape
bonusActions.effect: Polymorphs into any Small or Medium creature while retaining game statistics except size. Ends at 0 HP or when it uses a bonus action to end it.

reactions.name: Uncanny Dodge
reactions.trigger: An attacker the corrupter can see hits it with an attack.
reactions.effect: Halves that attack’s damage against the corrupter.

items.name: Omens of Apocalypse
items.summary: Two d12 campaign tables for apocalyptic warnings and calamities, including an explicit wild-magic/dead-magic spellcasting rule.

rawJson.name: Omens of Apocalypse
rawJson.summary: Two d12 campaign tables for apocalyptic warnings and calamities, including an explicit wild-magic/dead-magic spellcasting rule.

warningsD12.omen: A large star or comet appears at night and emits light comparable to a full moon.
A constant stream of meteors is visible day and night, all moving in the same direction.
The sky becomes an unnatural sickly green or bruised purple.
Water in a river, lake, or coastal region becomes blood, acid, or blue sand.
Creatures born on a particular day share an uncanny feature such as incandescent eyes, a fiery halo, or glowing blood.
Locusts, cicadas, wasps, spiders, snakes, or similar creatures gather in overwhelming swarms.
Earthquakes become increasingly frequent and strong.
A warning message appears across a city’s walls in countless languages.
A hermit from local legend arrives in town to deliver a warning.
A dead angel falls like a fireball, leaving a charred skeleton, burnt wings, and a scorched trumpet.
Everyone experiences the same warning dream.
All children stop what they are doing and deliver the same warning in unison.

calamitiesD12.calamity: The tarrasque awakens; a kraken, empyrean, or another titan can fill the same role.
A deadly plague resistant to curative magic sweeps the land.
A prolonged drought creates terrible famine.
A volcano or chain of volcanoes erupts.
A large asteroid crashes into the world.
A vast sinkhole swallows a city into the Underdark or a Lower Plane, or releases hordes of Fiends.
The gods lose their power and are forced into mortal forms.
The world is physically drawn into another plane of existence.
The gods war among themselves or against tremendously powerful alien beings.
Magic becomes unstable: wild-magic zones and dead-magic zones appear.
calamitiesD12.explicitRule: In a wild-magic zone, casting any spell of 1st level or higher causes a roll on the Player’s Handbook Wild Magic Surge table; dead-magic zones function like Antimagic Field on a larger scale.

calamitiesD12.calamity: The corpse of a slain god falls to the world.
All Dragons are consumed by unthinking rage and devastate nearby regions.

items.name: Advanced Detention Drone
items.summary: BMT Shield Guardian–derived flying detention drone with Regeneration, Spell Storing, protective reaction, and Detention Orb confinement.

rawJson.name: Advanced Detention Drone
rawJson.summary: BMT Shield Guardian–derived flying detention drone with Regeneration, Spell Storing, protective reaction, and Detention Orb confinement.

languages: understands commands given in any language but cannot speak

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.effect: Regains 10 HP at start of its turn if it has at least 1 HP.

traits.name: Spell Storing
traits.effect: A spellcaster wearing the associated guardian amulet can store one spell of 4th level or lower by casting it on the drone. The spell has no immediate effect and remains stored until replaced or cast. When commanded or when a predefined situation occurs, the drone casts the stored spell using the original caster’s parameters and maintaining concentration if required.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.effect: Makes two Fist attacks.

actions.name: Detention Orb
actions.failure: Creature is encased in a force orb just large enough to contain it. While encased it need not breathe, eat, or drink and does not age; nothing can pass through the orb, and teleportation/planar travel cannot enter or exit it.
actions.destroy: A successful Dispel Magic cast on the orb against DC 15 destroys it. Otherwise it lasts until the drone spends an action to end it or the drone is destroyed.
actions.limit: A drone can maintain only one detention orb; creating another causes the first to disappear and frees its occupant.

reactions.name: Shield
reactions.trigger: A creature attacks the wearer of the guardian amulet while the wearer is within 5 feet of the drone.
reactions.effect: Grants the wearer +2 AC against that attack.

actions.summary: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check to stanch the wound; magical healing also closes it.

traits.summary: The yochlol can use its action to polymorph into a form resembling a female drow or giant spider, or back into its true form. Its statistics are the same in each form. Equipment is not transformed, and it reverts to its true form if it dies.

traits.summary: The yochlol can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.summary: Charisma is the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14). At will: detect thoughts, web. 1/day: dominate person. No material components are required.

traits.name: Web Walker

actions.name: Mist Form
actions.summary: The yochlol transforms into toxic mist or reverts to its true form; worn or carried equipment transforms with it, and it reverts if it dies. In mist form it is incapacitated and can't speak, has a 30-foot flying speed and can hover, can pass through non-airtight spaces, has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws, and is immune to nonmagical damage. It can enter and stop in another creature's space; a creature that starts its turn sharing the space must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn, and while poisoned this way it is incapacitated.
